reason: E1 and E2 confirm that laser cladding of RHEA on TC4 is feasible and can improve properties, but neither provides evidence for a ductile FCC phase, suppression of defects via parameter optimization, or preservation of substrate ductility. The cited passages only loosely support the general concept, leaving most specific premises unsupported.
premises: Laser cladding can produce a metallurgically bonded, fine-grained RHEA coating on TC4
RHEA coatings exhibit high hardness and wear resistance due to high-entropy, lattice distortion, and cocktail effects
A minor FCC phase in the coating enhances ductility
Optimized laser parameters can suppress detrimental intermetallics, residual stresses, and cracking
The coating preserves the beneficial properties (ductility, bonding) of the TC4 substrate
